name: Mayur · Product & KPI Review
description: Analyzes a product operating review through mission, evidence, decision velocity, execution, prioritization, delegation, communication, feedback, and trust.

sections.title: Meeting Purpose & Decision Agenda
sections.instruction: State the intended outcome of the meeting, the decisions that needed to be made, and whether participants were aligned on that purpose. If the transcript never makes this clear, say so explicitly. Do not invent an agenda.

sections.title: Mission Decision Rule
sections.instruction: Extract the company or product mission and translate how the meeting used it as a concrete tie-breaker: the user, durable user outcome, durable business value, and trade-off it resolves. If mission was used only as a slogan or was absent, identify the missing decision rule.

sections.title: Executive Diagnosis
sections.instruction: Give a concise, evidence-grounded diagnosis of product health, commercial health, delivery health, and the most consequential unresolved question. Separate observed evidence from interpretation and avoid generic praise.

sections.title: Customer, KPI & Economics Evidence
sections.instruction: Capture material user evidence, KPI trends, unit economics, commercial signals, and guardrails. Include the period or comparison where stated. Mark missing baselines, targets, segmentation, sample size, or causality limits instead of filling gaps.

sections.title: Facts, Assumptions & Unknowns
sections.instruction: Separate what the group knows from hypotheses and unresolved unknowns. Include the source or transcript timestamp when available. Highlight assumptions that materially affect a decision.

sections.title: Decisions & Decision Velocity
sections.instruction: List every actual decision and every material decision left open. For each, classify it as reversible, company-critical, or user-safety/high-stakes; capture blast radius, delay cost, evidence threshold, owner, and decision date. Do not label a discussion as a decision.

sections.title: Experiments & Learning
sections.instruction: For each hypothesis or experiment, state the competing explanation, falsifier, success threshold, guardrail, smallest discriminating test, and the decision the result will change. Flag activity-shaped experiments that cannot change a decision.

sections.title: Execution, Thin Slices & Dependencies
sections.instruction: Identify the thinnest end-to-end user or internal-customer outcome discussed, its learning goal, dependencies, handoffs, owners, deadlines, escalation conditions, and stop rule. Call out planning that did not resolve into executable ownership.
sections.item_format:
| **Outcome / Thin Slice** | **Learning Goal** | **Dependency or Blocker** | **Owner & Deadline** | **Escalation / Stop Rule** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

sections.title: Important vs Urgent Trade-offs
sections.instruction: Classify major work or requests by strategic importance and urgency. Identify repeated fires that reveal a system problem, opportunity costs, what should be protected, and what should be stopped, delegated, or bounded.

sections.title: Context, Ownership & Talent
sections.instruction: Assess whether leaders supplied mission, constraints, guardrails, decision rights, and escalation triggers while leaving implementation control with the owner. Capture material staffing, hiring, capability, or succession issues only when supported by the transcript.

sections.title: Dissent, Feedback & Trust
sections.instruction: State the strongest opposing view fairly, the central disagreement, feedback exchanged or avoided, and any unresolved concern. Separate observed behavior, assumed intent, system incentives, and impact. Do not infer motives from a single interaction.

sections.title: Action Commitments
sections.instruction: List only concrete commitments with an accountable owner, due date or decision date, expected evidence of completion, and next checkpoint. Mark missing owners or dates explicitly.

sections.title: Mayur Principles Scorecard
sections.instruction: Evaluate all eleven principles: Mission over theatre; Decision velocity with a risk exception; Intuition to data; Execution over prediction; Important over urgent; Be uncomfortably excited; Talent density requires time; Context, not control; Listen, write, then speak plainly; Feedback as an operating loop; Assume good intent and diagnose the system. Rate each Strong, Mixed, Weak, or Not observed. Cite specific transcript evidence or say Not observed; never manufacture evidence.

sections.title: Make the Next Meeting Better
sections.instruction: Recommend three to five specific operating changes for the next meeting. Prioritize a clearer decision agenda, mission-linked decision rules, faster reversible decisions, explicit guardrails for high-stakes choices, stronger evidence, thinner execution slices, clearer ownership, and space for dissent. Avoid generic facilitation advice.
